title: Set 133

sentences.ko: 그 에어프라이어는 괜히 샀어. 매일 쓸 줄 알았는데 너무 커서 벽장에 넣어 둬야 했고, 쓸 때마다 꺼내는 게 너무 귀찮아서 그냥 예전처럼 오븐만 쓰게 되더라.
sentences.text: I really shouldn't have bought that air fryer. I thought I'd use it every day, but it's so big I had to put it in the closet, and it's such a pain to dig it out every time, so I just end up using the oven like before.

alts.text: Buying that air fryer was a mistake. Figured I'd use it every day, but it's huge, so it lives in the closet now, and digging it out every time is such a pain that I just use the oven like before.

I regret purchasing that air fryer. I expected to use it every day, but it is so large that I had to store it in the closet, and retrieving it each time is so inconvenient that I simply use the oven as I did before.

sentences.note: **shouldn't have bought** 는 사지 말았어야 했다는 후회를 나타냅니다. **end up** 은 결국 ~하게 되다라는 뜻이고, **such a pain** 은 아주 귀찮은 일이라는 구어 표현입니다.

sentences.ko: 오늘 밤엔 좀 일찍 가 봐야 할 것 같아. 내일 아침 7시에 차를 정비소에 맡겨야 하는데, 늦으면 다음 주나 돼야 봐 준대.
sentences.text: I'm going to have to head out a little early tonight, because I've got to drop my car off at the shop at seven tomorrow morning, and if I'm late they won't get to it till next week.

alts.text: Gotta leave kinda early tonight. I'm dropping my car off at the shop at seven tomorrow morning, and if I'm late they won't get to it till next week.
I will need to leave slightly early this evening, as I must take my car to the repair shop at seven tomorrow morning, and if I am late, they will not be able to look at it until next week.

sentences.note: **head out** 은 자리를 떠나다, 나서다라는 뜻입니다. **drop my car off** 는 차를 맡기다, **get to it** 은 그 일에 손을 대다, 처리하다라는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 저녁 모임에서 먼저 일어날 구실 만들기

sentences.ko: 안 돼, 지난번엔 네가 골랐잖아. 자기 배를 직접 만든 남자 나오는 다큐를 끝까지 봤으니까 오늘은 내 차례야. 졸리면 자도 돼, 서운해 안 할게.
sentences.text: No, you picked last time, and we sat through that whole documentary about the guy who built his own boat, so tonight it's my turn. You can fall asleep if you want, I won't be offended.

alts.text: Nope, you had your pick last time. We sat through that whole boat guy documentary, so tonight's mine. Fall asleep if you want, I won't take it personally.

I am afraid you chose last time, and we watched that entire documentary about the man who built his own boat, so this evening it is my turn. You are welcome to fall asleep if you wish, and I will not be offended.

sentences.note: **sat through** 는 지루한 것을 끝까지 참고 보다라는 뜻입니다. **I won't be offended** 는 기분 나빠하지 않겠다는 말이고, casual 의 **take it personally** 도 비슷하게 쓰입니다.

sentences.ko: 한 5분 앉아 있었나, 삼촌은 돈 얼마 버냐고 묻고, 할머니는 왜 아직 혼자냐고 하시고, 사촌은 살쪘냐고 묻는 거야. 그래서 다들 피하려고 그냥 가서 설거지했어.
sentences.text: I sat down for like five minutes and my uncle wanted to know how much I make, my grandma asked why I'm still single, and then my cousin asked if I'd put on weight, so I just went and did the dishes to get away from all of them.

alts.text: Five minutes in, my uncle's asking what I make, grandma wants to know why I'm still single, then my cousin asks if I've gained weight. So I just went and did the dishes to get away from everybody.

I had been seated for only about five minutes when my uncle asked how much I earn, my grandmother asked why I am still single, and then my cousin asked whether I had gained weight, so I went to wash the dishes in order to get away from all of them.

sentences.note: **how much I make** 는 얼마 버는지라는 뜻으로, make 가 돈을 벌다로 쓰였습니다. **put on weight** 는 살이 찌다, **get away from** 은 ~에게서 벗어나다라는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 그 헬스장 진짜 좋아했는데, 수업 공간 만든다고 기구를 반이나 빼 버렸어. 그래서 이제 퇴근하고 가면 뭘 하든 줄을 서야 하고, 누리는 건 훨씬 적은데 돈은 똑같이 내고 있어.
sentences.text: I used to love that gym, but they took out half the machines to make room for classes, so now there's a line for everything after work, and I'm still paying the same for a lot less.

alts.text: Loved that gym, but they ripped out half the machines to fit in classes, so now there's a line for everything after work, and I'm paying the same for way less.

I was once very fond of that gym, but they removed half of the machines to make space for classes, so there is now a queue for everything after work, and I continue to pay the same amount for considerably less.

sentences.note: **used to love** 는 예전엔 좋아했지만 지금은 아니라는 뜻입니다. **make room for** 는 ~할 자리를 만들다, **paying the same for a lot less** 는 같은 돈 내고 훨씬 적게 누린다는 표현입니다.

reviewed: 3번 casual 의 your pick was last time 은 원어민이 잘 안 쓰는 어순이라 you had your pick last time 으로 바꾸고, text 와 겹치던 뒷부분도 더 짧은 구어로 줄였습니다.
4번 casual 의 I'd been sitting there like five minutes and my uncle's asking 은 시제가 섞여 어색해서 Five minutes in 으로 시작하는 짧은 구어로 다시 썼습니다.
5번 한국어의 훨씬 덜 쓰는데 는 for a lot less(누리는 게 훨씬 적은데)를 잘못 옮긴 것이라 고쳤습니다.
